title: spot-preempt-rotation-scratchpad
content:
Goal: Capture breadcrumbs for recurring failures when spot/preemptible nodes are rotated (k3s & GKE mixed clusters). Personal scratchpad — messy, steps tried, hypotheses, and next actions.

Summary of incident series (quick):
- Symptoms: ~5-10% of spot nodes fail to rejoin after termination/replacement. Pods stuck Pending or CrashLoopBackOff in kube-system and app namespaces. Intermittent image unpack failures and CSI volume attach timeouts.
- Scope: repro across two clusters: dev-k3s (edge) and staging-gke (preemptible).
- Likely culprits: cloud-init timing, node kubelet config drift, missing tolerations/taints, containerd image unpack errors on small instance types, ephemeral disk attach race.

Chronology / commands I ran (with notable outputs):
1) Check node state right after AWS ASG/GCP preempt event:
   kubectl get nodes -o wide
   # saw nodes in NotReady or Ready,SchedulingDisabled for a short window

2) Inspect node events:
   kubectl describe node ip-10-0-7-92.us-west-2.compute.internal
   # Events: NodeAllocatableEnforced, kubelet has disk pressure then Ready

3) Look at kubelet logs for the node (ssh -> journalctl):
   sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p'
   # Repeated: "Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to unpack layer: write /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd... no space left on device"

4) containerd diagnostics:
   sudo crictl --runtime-endpoint unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock ps -a
   sudo crictl images | wc -l
   # image cache > 300 on t3.small -> OOM-ish / disk pressure

5) Helm issues for CNI and storage: During node join, daemonset pods CrashLoopBackOff
   kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | egrep 'calico|aws-ebs-csi'
   kubectl logs -n kube-system ds/calico-node -c calico-node --tail=100
   # calico failing to start: failed to open iptables lock -> permission/namespace timing

6) PVC attach errors (EBS/GCE PD):
   kubectl get pvc -A | grep Bound
   kubectl describe pod <stuck-pod> -n app-namespace
   # Events: Multi-Attach error or AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-...": volume is already attached to ...
   # or: "AttachVolume operation failed for volume ...: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded"

Quick hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: New node boots and kubelet registers before cloud-init finishes mounting block devices -> container runtime runs out of space or mounts happen after kubelet tries to schedule pods.
- H2: Image cache on small instance types fills /var/lib -> containerd can't unpack images for system pods (calico, coredns) leading to daemons not ready.
- H3: During preempt replacement, kube-controller-manager races and tries to reattach PDs before detach completes, causing Multi-Attach errors that leave PVCs stuck.
- H4: Missing tolerations on some helm charts (for node.kubernetes.io/preemptible) or taint handling causing critical system pods to not be scheduled on new spot nodes.

What I've tried (and results):
- Added a cloud-init step to expand disk and pre-populate image cache (docker pull of common images) -> reduced frequency but not fixed (still some attach timeouts).
- Adjusted kubelet --eviction-hard thresholds (memory.available<100Mi) on small instances -> fewer OOMs but didn't help attach errors.
- For GKE preemptible cluster: increased node termination grace and used node auto-repair disabled during repro tests -> helped for PD detach race but not fully.
- Helm: added toleration for "preemptible" taint to critical daemonsets (calico, aws-ebs-csi) -> improved scheduling but image-unpack still showed up.
- Cleaned image cache on nodes in temp: sudo crictl rmi $(crictl images -q) -> temporary fix; needs automated housekeeping.

Notable error paste snippets (copied for search):
- "failed to unpack layer: write /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/...: no space left on device"
- "error attaching volume "pvc-xxxxxxxx": Multi-Attach error for volume"
- "error while mounting volume /var/lib/kubelet/pods/...: mount failed: exit status 32"
- "failed to sync node status: timed out waiting for the condition"

Ideas / next experiments (TODO list):
- [ ] Repro run with cloud-init verbose logs and systemd-analyze blame to confirm timing between mounts and kubelet start. (Add a delay for kubelet service start via cloud-init to test H1).
- [ ] Add a node-boot hook that clears image cache and pulls required images (prerender pull list) and measure incidence. -> create a small userdata script.
- [ ] Update helm charts to include tolerations and nodeSelector for critical system DS (test in staging). Backport to infra repo if positive.
- [ ] For PD attach race: add a controller fallback or longer timeout; test kube-controller-manager flag adjustments on a control-plane replica. File follow-up JIRA if we need infra change.
- [ ] Automate image GC on small instance types (systemd timer) and set containerd/gc thresholds.
- [ ] Add more observability: record node provisioning timeline in metrics (node_boot_started, mounts_ready, kubelet_started, kubelet_ready).

Notes-to-self / Useful one-liners to run during next repro:
- ssh into problem node: sudo journalctl -u cloud-init -n 200 --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p'
- check mounts: findmnt -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,OPTIONS
- check disk usage by dir: sudo du -sh /var/lib/* | sort -h | tail -n 20
- containerd snapshot count: sudo find /var/lib/containerd -maxdepth 2 -type d | wc -l
- quick image unblock: sudo systemctl stop kubelet && sudo crictl rmi --prune && sudo systemctl start kubelet

Slack threads / people to ping: @maya (Maya Chen) has seen similar on edge clusters, @ravi for PV/CSI context. File JIRA-CLOUD-3421 for tracking infra fixes.

Longer-term ideas (brainstorm):
- Build a small init container that runs pre-pull + healthcheck and marks a node condition when done; use node auto-replace health gating to prevent scheduling until image priming complete.
- For PDs, create a short locking controller that ensures proper detach complete across zones before reattach (or rely on cloud provider detach retries).

Random notes / fragments (copied from terminal during triage):
- "kubelet[1234]: E1123 10:11:12.345678  1234 kubelet.go:1981] Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to unpack layer: ... no space left on device"
- "cloud-init[1]: Mounted EBS volume but not updated /etc/fstab -> ephemeral mount lost on reboot"

If I can't fix this in infra: plan fallback: pin critical workloads to dedicated non-spot node pools and route traffic via ingress weight shift.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate while running repros next week.
